subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches inside plugin hook, plugin skill, and sandbox containment checks for the Windows performance win?
rationale: The linked fix avoids the unsafe process-wide cache shape, but it still changes cache lifetime in boundary-sensitive realpath checks, so maintainer security-boundary intent is needed before this issue can close through the PR.

options.title: Accept Operation-Scoped Caches
options.body: Land the linked PR after normal review and proof, treating per-operation cache lifetime as the accepted performance/security tradeoff.

options.title: Restrict To Non-Containment Hot Paths
options.body: Keep the manifest-registry optimization and reject caching inside plugin and sandbox containment checks until a narrower design exists.

options.title: Pause For Cache Contract Design
options.body: Leave this issue and PR open while maintainers define an explicit cache-lifetime contract for fs-safe boundary helpers.

recommendation.title: Accept Operation-Scoped Caches
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after normal review and proof, treating per-operation cache lifetime as the accepted performance/security tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the linked PR and has recent merged work in the affected sandbox, skill, and manifest-registry cache surfaces.
